## Chiloé Island: what to see and why visit

Chiloé lies in Chile's Los Lagos Region, south of Puerto Montt. Its main island, Isla Grande de Chiloé, is surrounded by smaller islands and sea channels. Fishing villages, wooden houses, green hills and churches built by local carpenters stand side by side. The islanders' cultural traditions were shaped by Indigenous communities and European missions.

For visitors, the principal difference between Chiloé and the neighboring Lake District is island life. In many settlements the sea historically determined transport, livelihoods and where houses were built. The northern port town of [Ancud](/chile/place/ancud/) is a convenient starting point; a longer journey can include the central archipelago, wooden churches and natural areas.

Chiloé can form part of a broader [Chile itinerary](/chile/) or be explored over several dedicated days. When choosing a duration, distinguish a one-day trip to the northern island from a journey through multiple settlements and islands.

## Northern and central Chiloé: different experiences

| Area | Reasons to visit |
|---|---|
| Ancud | Port history, fort, crafts |
| Castro | Stilt houses and urban culture |
| Dalcahue and Quinchao | Wooden churches and villages |
| West coast | Forest, ocean, wildlife observation |

In northern Chiloé, [Ancud](/chile/place/ancud/) offers a look into Spanish fortifications, crafts and local legends. In a suitable season and with favorable sea conditions, a visit to the [bird colonies of Puñihuil](/chile/place/punihuil-penguin-colony/) is possible from this area. This is a separate nature excursion whose time should not automatically be added to a short city tour.

In the central archipelago lie Castro and settlements associated with wooden architecture. Castro is known for its colorful stilt houses, called *palafitos*, while churches and workshops survive in towns around bays and channels. Plan stops and drives separately if you want to explore these places closely.

## Wooden churches and UNESCO heritage

One of Chiloé's best-known features is its wooden churches. **Sixteen churches of the archipelago were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2000.** They are distributed among different settlements, including Castro, Dalcahue, Chonchi, Achao and smaller islands. They are **not sixteen attractions within one city** or one complex with a shared admission gate.

Local builders used boatbuilding skills, timber and traditional joinery. The architecture blends European religious forms with local construction techniques. It makes more sense to plan an itinerary around several chosen churches than to try to cover the entire archipelago in one day. Access to the interiors of active churches must be arranged locally; religious activities and the condition of each monument affect visits.

The cultural experience extends beyond churches. Woolen handicrafts, woodworking, seafood cuisine and island legends all help explain life on Chiloé. A tasting, workshop visit or church admission is included in a particular tour only when explicitly listed in its program.

## Chiloé's natural environment and penguin watching

The west coast faces the Pacific, while the interior is known for humid forests and small settlements. Set aside a separate nature day if you want to explore woodland areas. For seabird watching, travelers often choose [Puñihuil near Ancud](/chile/place/punihuil-penguin-colony/), where Magellanic and Humboldt penguins nest on rocky islets.

Ancud's municipal tourism service gives an approximate boat-watching season **from September to March**. Departures also depend on wind, waves and authorization to sail. The birds are observed from the water without landing at nesting sites. Even in the right month, neither a boat departure nor a sighting of a specified number of penguins is guaranteed.

Rain is possible on Chiloé throughout the year. Pack a waterproof jacket, footwear for wet paths and a spare warm layer. The southern summer, December to February, has longer days, but it would be wrong to describe the island as having a completely dry season.

## Getting to Chiloé

The most common overland route passes through [Puerto Varas](/chile/place/puerto-varas/) and Puerto Montt to the mainland ferry terminal at Pargua. Cars and passengers then cross the [Chacao Channel](/chile/place/chacao-strait/) by ferry and arrive in the north of the island. Chile's official tourism portal indicates that the crossing itself usually takes about **30 minutes**; waiting to board and onward driving need separate allowances.

Another possibility is a flight to Mocopulli Airport near Castro, provided suitable services are available. For travelers focused on the wooden churches of the central archipelago, this arrival may be more convenient than a long overland route from the mainland. Check current flights, ferry schedules and travel times for the chosen dates.

## How many days to allow and which program to choose

**One day** works for an introduction to northern Chiloé: the crossing, Ancud and return. It does not leave time for all the famous churches, central towns and nature parks.

**Two to three days or more** allow a combination of northern Chiloé, Castro and several historic villages. More time is needed to discover smaller islands, forests, crafts and natural areas without constant rushing.

Our ["VIP: 33-Day Grand Tour of South America"](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/) includes an excursion from Puerto Varas: ferry across Chacao, visit to Ancud and return. Puñihuil is listed as a stop **when weather permits**. See the [Chiloé and Ancud excursion](/chile/chiloe-island/chiloe-ancud-chacao-day-trip/) for the details of that day. The itinerary does not promise a separate multi-day journey visiting every wooden church.

## Frequently asked questions about Chiloé

### Is Chiloé one island or an archipelago?

Both terms are used in different contexts. Isla Grande is the main island, and the Chiloé Archipelago contains many smaller islands. Some of the famous wooden churches are not on the main island.

### Can I visit Chiloé on a day trip from Puerto Varas?

Yes. There is an excursion to the northern island, including [Ancud](/chile/place/ancud/). Allow time for the road journey, ferry crossings both ways and sightseeing. Central Chiloé and the smaller islands need additional time.

### Where can I see penguins on Chiloé?

Near the [Puñihuil islets](/chile/place/punihuil-penguin-colony/) by Ancud. The usual viewing period is September to March, but boat excursions depend on weather and sea conditions.

### Are all the UNESCO wooden churches in Ancud?

The sixteen protected churches are spread among settlements across the archipelago. Ancud has a museum devoted to the heritage, but a museum visit is not the same as traveling to the churches.

## Chile's Colchagua Valley: wineries, tastings and itineraries

Colchagua Valley lies in central [Chile](/chile/) and is known for red wines, vineyards and winery visits. Rows of vines cover flat areas and hillsides, while tastings take place at estates that can differ greatly in history, size and winemaking approach.

Colchagua offers an opportunity to explore one wine region in depth. In one day, visitors can discover an individual estate and its grape varieties; over several days, they can compare different styles of red wine, enjoy regional food and stay around Santa Cruz. Simply visiting the valley, however, does not confirm an appointment at any specific winery: tastings must be arranged in advance.

## Which wines are made in Colchagua?

The region is especially noted for **Carménère** and **Cabernet Sauvignon**. Carménère originally came from France but became widely grown in Chile, where it is now one of the country's recognizable varieties. Its wines are often described as having dark-fruit, herbal and spicy notes, though exact aromas depend on the estate, vintage and aging.

Cabernet Sauvignon is known for full-bodied, structured red wines, while blends allow estates to produce a variety of styles. It is more interesting to compare several wines from one winery than just the names on labels: a young and an aged wine, a single-varietal example and a blend.

During tastings, guests often consider aroma, acidity, tannins and finish. These characteristics explain differences between wines more precisely than a general judgment such as "tasty" or "famous." If you do not drink alcohol, the scenery, estate history, vineyards and food can still make the journey worthwhile; the availability of an alcohol-free program must be checked separately.

## Choosing a winery

| Aim | Format to look for |
|---|---|
| First introduction | Estate overview and a basic tasting |
| Comparing varieties | Themed red-wine tasting |
| Gastronomy | Wine and a paired lunch |
| Learning about production | Winery production tour |

Each winery has its own booking rules, available capacity, duration and visiting programs. Some emphasize vineyard management, others cellars, collections and wine pairings with regional cuisine. It is better to turn a shortlist of appealing wineries into a realistic route accounting for driving time than to attempt all of them in one day.

Historically well-known names in the region include **Montes, Casa Silva and Viu Manent**. Their presence in Colchagua is documented by national tourism materials, but this does not mean that our tours automatically include these wineries. Confirm which estates are open to visitors on your dates for the particular itinerary.

Some wineries offer tastings in several languages. Guiding arrangements, specific wines, transport and meals must follow the confirmed quote, not assumptions based on a vineyard photograph.

## Santa Cruz and the valley's cultural attractions

**Santa Cruz** often serves as a base for a wine journey. Beyond tastings, it offers local architecture and culture from central Chile. Colchagua therefore appeals to those who want to combine wineries with a relaxed walk, lunch and time in a smaller town.

Staying overnight in the region eliminates the need to return to Santiago after a full day of tastings. This is especially useful if several wineries or a long gastronomic lunch are planned. After tasting wine, use an agreed transfer and avoid driving yourself.

When selecting a program, decide what interests you most: learning about production, tasting different reds or spending a day among vineyards. These activities overlap but require different pacing and numbers of stops.

## The best season to visit Colchagua

The grape-growing cycle in the Southern Hemisphere differs from that in Europe. Harvest falls mainly in late summer and early autumn, usually **February through April**, depending on variety, estate and weather. Harvest celebrations, called **vendimia**, traditionally occur in this season, including in the Santa Cruz area. A specific festival requires checking that year's calendar.

At other times, wineries may operate regular visitor programs, though the nature of the experience changes. Summer can be hot in open vineyards; spring and autumn may be more comfortable for long walks, while winter landscapes and winery operations look different. Confirm availability, weather and visitor rules.

If you want to see production work during harvest, do not assume guests can enter operational areas freely. Access depends on the winery's arrangements and a visit agreed in advance.

## Getting there from Santiago and allowing enough time

Chile's national tourism portal identifies Colchagua as a wine valley reached from Santiago by road to the south, mainly along Ruta 5 Sur. Distance and time depend on the chosen winery. The Santa Cruz area is approximately **180 km** from the capital, and the journey takes a few hours depending on traffic and stops.

A day trip from Santiago can work for one sightseeing excursion, but consider staying overnight if several wineries are the goal. This allows unhurried tastings without cutting each one short for the return transfer.

**Colchagua, Maipo and Casablanca are different wine valleys.** They can be alternatives or separate stops on a longer central Chile itinerary, but should not be grouped under one name. Casablanca is often chosen for white wines, while Colchagua is known for fuller-bodied reds; the final choice depends on travelers' interests.

## Colchagua on Ada Tours journeys

On our [17-day grand tour of Chile and Argentina](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/), the wine day in central Chile considers Maipo, Colchagua and Casablanca. These are **possible wine areas** in the program, so a visit specifically to Colchagua or to any individual winery depends on the chosen itinerary and is not guaranteed by the tour's title.

Travelers primarily interested in vineyards and cuisine can explore [food and wine journeys](/interests/food-and-wine/) and decide how long the wine section should last. To combine wine with nature and historic cities, allocate some days to other regions of Chile.

## Frequently asked questions about Colchagua Valley

### What wines is Colchagua known for?

Primarily red wines made from Carménère and Cabernet Sauvignon. Styles vary between wineries, so a themed tasting helps compare grape varieties and production techniques.

### Can I visit Colchagua from Santiago in one day?

Yes, but allow several hours of road travel each way, plus distances between estates and time for tours. For several wineries, a paired lunch and a relaxed visit to Santa Cruz, staying overnight is more convenient.

### When is the grape harvest?

Usually in late Chilean summer and early autumn, approximately February–April. Dates depend on the weather, grapes and winery; harvest festivals have separate calendars.

## Adding Colchagua wine country to a Chile itinerary

[Colchagua Valley](/chile/place/colchagua-valley/) is known for vineyards and red-wine tastings. It is one of central Chile's wine destinations that can be considered when arranging a private itinerary from [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/).

On the existing [17-day private grand tour of Chile and Argentina](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/), day two is dedicated to vineyards. Winery visits, tastings and an overnight stay at VIK Chile in Millahue are planned. **Maipo, Colchagua and Casablanca are possible areas** for that wine day, while the exact wineries and valleys are agreed before travel.

This is the essential distinction: **a wine day is part of the program, but a visit specifically to Colchagua is not guaranteed**. If you wish to visit this valley, it should be explicitly included in the confirmed itinerary along with the selected winery and tasting time.

## Why choose Colchagua?

Colchagua belongs to central Chile's wine-producing regions. Chile Travel, the national tourism portal, highlights winery tastings and food pairings in the area, especially for the red varieties Carménère and Cabernet Sauvignon. Santa Cruz is a useful reference point for local culture and wineries.

An estate visit might involve walking through vineyards, learning about production and tasting wine. **None of those elements is automatically included in every tour mentioning Colchagua**: the particular winery, its schedule and the agreed package determine the visit.

As part of a longer South American journey, Colchagua offers a chance to spend time among vines before the route shifts to very different landscapes: [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/), the Atacama Desert, Patagonia and Argentina. For serious wine enthusiasts, selecting the tasting format in advance matters more than simply recording the valley as a geographic stop.

## Wine day: Colchagua, Maipo or Cachapoal?

The 17-day itinerary has an important geographic distinction. **VIK Chile is in Millahue, in the Cachapoal Valley**, while Colchagua is among the possible wine regions under discussion. The hotel's name therefore provides no evidence that the journey must pass through Colchagua.

| Area | What to clarify |
|---|---|
| Colchagua | Winery and tasting |
| Maipo | Route from Santiago |
| Cachapoal | Stay in Millahue |
| Casablanca | Alternative wine day |

This is not a list of four included stops. It helps choose the wine region that suits the traveler, the road journey and the hotels already planned. The itinerary does not promise to visit all four valleys in a single day.

Private transport is offered for the wine day; the description mentions helicopter and road-transfer options, but the transport actually used and its cost must be linked to the selected wineries. Do not assume the same one-hour flight applies to every possible valley.

## Agreeing on Colchagua without overloading the itinerary

Begin with your priority: a particular winery, a comparative tasting or a gastronomic lunch. Then decide whether that replaces part of the existing wine day or requires a change to its duration. If an estate lies far from the convenient transfer route, adjusting the sequence of stops is wiser than rushing every tasting.

On the [17-day grand tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/), long-distance flights and transfers follow the central Chile section. Changes to the wine day should therefore be agreed **before** finalizing flights and accommodation. The inclusion of a specific estate, guiding, dinner and transport must be reflected in the individual offer. Payment conditions and included services follow the agreed version.

If you want wine to be the main purpose of the journey, compare other [gastronomic itineraries](/interests/food-and-wine/) rather than choosing a long multi-country trip for a single day.

## Frequently asked questions about Colchagua as an optional stop

### Is Colchagua already included in the 17-day tour?

The wine day is included, but Colchagua is one of several possible regions. The specific valley and winery must be agreed and added to the itinerary.

### Is VIK Chile in Colchagua?

No. In the published itinerary, VIK Chile is in Millahue, Cachapoal Valley. It is part of a neighboring wine region, not a reason to misidentify the hotel's location.

### Can I select the winery in advance?

Yes. A particular estate can be discussed when arranging the private itinerary. Availability, time and services need confirmation, and the selected winery must appear in the offer.

### Is there a separate fixed price for adding Colchagua?

The [grand tour description](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/) does not give a universal surcharge for Colchagua. The cost depends on the selected estates, transport and contents of the day.

## Concha y Toro: exploring Chilean wine in the Maipo Valley

The Concha y Toro winery is in Pirque, south of [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), in the Maipo wine region. Visitors come for its vineyards, historic estate, cellars and tastings, and for one of Chilean winemaking's best-known stories: the legend of **Casillero del Diablo**.

A visit combines a walk through the grounds and vines with an introduction to wine production. It is a convenient introduction to [Chile's wine journeys](/interests/food-and-wine/), especially when a trip passes through the capital and there is time for at least part of a day outside the city.

## About the winery

Concha y Toro is an active wine brand with a history linked to the Maipo Valley. Its visitor center is at Pirque, where estate buildings and historic spaces survive alongside the vineyards. The area has views across green vines to the mountains.

The official visitor center offers several tour options. Depending on the chosen ticket, they may include the gardens, vineyard, historic cellars, tastings and food experiences. **Not every ticket covers all these elements**, and the contents vary by rate and season.

Visitors interested in how grape varieties, aging and winemakers' decisions affect flavor will gain more from a tour with production explanations than from merely walking around the attractive grounds.

## The Casillero del Diablo legend

The name Casillero del Diablo, often translated as "Devil's Cellar," is associated with a long-standing story. According to the winery's own account, Don Melchor Concha y Toro spread rumors about strange happenings in the cellars to discourage theft of the wines stored there. The legend became part of the brand's identity.

During a visit to the historic cellar, travelers can learn why this story became associated with the wine and how it is used today. It is **a marketing legend with a historical origin**, not a claim that supernatural events occurred.

The cellar itself is also interesting. Storage conditions, barrels, cool air and the organization of a winery help connect the legend with the winemakers' work.

## How visits and tastings work

A tour may begin with a walk through the grounds and vineyards, then continue into historic rooms and a tasting space. The number of wine samples, guiding arrangements and meals included depend on the option reserved for the travel date.

The winery's official website lists premium tours, additional tastings and gastronomic experiences, among other products. Some focus on estate history, while others explore wines in greater depth.

| Format | What to expect |
|---|---|
| Overview | History and vineyards |
| With tasting | Comparing samples |
| Extended | More time in the cellars |
| Gastronomic | Wine and food |

Before purchasing a ticket, check the start time, guiding language, availability of the selected tasting, meals included and cancellation terms. The winery offers several programs, so an older description may differ from the current offer.

## Getting there from Santiago

Pirque lies in the Maipo Valley outside central Santiago. Concha y Toro's visitor center indicates that the trip from Santiago generally takes about **one hour**, though the actual duration depends on where you depart and traffic.

Arrange a driver, transfer or another option that avoids driving after wine tasting. If the trip includes several wineries, allow for journeys between them and the appointment times at each estate.

Nearby lies the [Maipo Valley](/chile/place/maipo-valley/), famous for vineyards and diverse wine routes. Concha y Toro, however, is **one particular winery**, not a name for the entire region; its terms and prices cannot be applied to neighboring estates.

## Concha y Toro on Ada Tours itineraries

On our ["Chile and Argentina with Mendoza Wine Region in Nine Days"](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-mendoza-wine-9-days/) itinerary, Concha y Toro is a distinct part of the Chilean section. Travelers explore the vineyards, grounds and winery, followed by a tasting.

Earlier, the journey covers Mendoza in Argentina and wineries in the Uco Valley. The comparison is valuable because of the differences: Malbec is widely associated with Mendoza, while Chile's Maipo Valley is particularly known for red wines, including Cabernet Sauvignon.

When booking, consult the specific program. The number of wines tasted, lunch arrangements and guiding language may differ by product. A Concha y Toro label on a bottle does not mean every Ada Tours package includes the historic visitor center in Pirque.

## Practical details and seasons

Vineyards look different throughout the year. During Southern Hemisphere summer, the vines are green; as harvest approaches, the landscape changes, and colder months bring work unlike the familiar images of grape bunches. If a particular stage of wine production matters to you, check whether it can be seen before traveling.

Comfortable shoes are useful on vineyard paths, with an extra layer for the cellar. Sun protection helps in open areas. Drink alcohol moderately, and check the current winery rules and legal requirements for minors.

## Frequently asked questions about Concha y Toro

### Where is the winery?

Its visitor center is in Pirque, in the Maipo Valley near Santiago de Chile. It requires a separate trip out of the city.

### Is tasting wine compulsory?

The format depends on the selected offer. Visitors can focus on history, gardens and winemaking; check conditions for minors and non-drinking guests when booking.

### Is Casillero del Diablo a separate winery?

It is a well-known wine label and legend associated with Concha y Toro's historic cellars. Whether the cellar is visited depends on the tour.

### Can I visit without reserving in advance?

The official winery offers online reservations. Selecting a program and confirming a time in advance is more reliable than assuming places will be available on arrival.

## Tours visiting Concha y Toro winery in Chile

[Concha y Toro winery](/chile/place/concha-y-toro/) is in Pirque, Maipo Valley, near [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). Visitors come to discover Chilean winemaking through walks among vineyards and estate gardens, the winery's history and tastings. For travelers choosing an existing itinerary, the key questions are **which day is devoted to the winery and which other wine regions the journey includes**.

This collection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} passing through Concha y Toro. The main linked itinerary is the [nine-day Argentina and Chile journey with Mendoza](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-mendoza-wine-9-days/). It allows travelers to compare the winemaking traditions of two countries: first the estates of Argentina's Mendoza region, then Concha y Toro near the Chilean capital. The winery visit is part of the main itinerary, not merely a suggestion for an optional activity on a free day.

## How Concha y Toro fits into the journey

On the [nine-day Argentina and Chile tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-mendoza-wine-9-days/), Concha y Toro is scheduled for **day eight**, after returning to the Santiago area. Travelers have breakfast at the hotel, then head to the vineyards. The program includes a walk through the grounds and gardens, an introduction to the winery and a tasting. Afterward, the group returns to Santiago; an airport transfer follows the next day.

**Lunch at the winery is paid for separately.** When comparing prices, examine both the overall tour rate and the list of included services. Additional tasting formats offered by the visitor center must not automatically be treated as part of the existing tour, since the contents depend on the actual booking.

Before the Chilean section, the itinerary passes through [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), [Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/) and the [Uco Valley](/argentina/place/uco-valley/). It combines cultural experiences, wineries and time in the cities. After Argentina's wine region, travelers explore [Valparaíso and Viña del Mar](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/), then spend a separate day at Concha y Toro.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_vinnyj_tur_v_argentinu_i_chili}}

## Comparing wine days in Argentina and Chile

A major advantage of this itinerary is the opportunity to experience two wine-producing regions without organizing two separate trips. [Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/) lies on the other side of the Andes and is known for its vineyards. Chile's [Maipo Valley](/chile/place/maipo-valley/) offers another perspective on winemaking, with estates and vineyards that welcome visitors near a major city.

Mendoza introduces a wine region, multiple estates and surrounding mountains. In Pirque, the main stop centers on one producer, Concha y Toro, its grounds, cellars and the story of the Casillero del Diablo label. The sequence turns tastings into a comparison of wine styles, winery practices and the visitor experience.

| Stop | Main focus |
|---|---|
| [Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/) | Region and various wineries |
| [Uco Valley](/argentina/place/uco-valley/) | Vineyards beneath the Andes |
| [Concha y Toro](/chile/place/concha-y-toro/) | Estate, cellars and tasting |

These visits should not be assumed to have identical duration or the same number of samples. Such details are set by each winery's program, not the general phrase "wine tour."

## Who will enjoy this journey?

This route is particularly attractive to travelers who want to combine gastronomy with South American cities and culture. It covers two major urban centers, Mendoza's wine region, Chilean vineyards and the Pacific coast. The trip has consecutive transfers and excursions, so view it as a busy itinerary rather than a vacation spent in one wine hotel.

Pay attention to guiding arrangements. The tour provides group excursions with **English-speaking guides**; Russian-speaking guides or interpreters are available for an extra charge. Replacing group services with private ones also requires separate agreement. If the guiding language is crucial, settle it when choosing the price option.

For tasting-focused journeys, compare [food and wine tours in Chile](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/chile/) or the entire [Chile tour catalog](/chile/tour/). These are separate collections and do not mean that every program necessarily visits Concha y Toro.

## Planning the winery day

Concha y Toro fits conveniently into a stay in Santiago because its visitor center is in the metropolitan region. Even so, traveling outside the city and tasting wine take a substantial part of the day. If onward flights follow the visit, keep a sensible buffer and avoid adding too many distant attractions to the same day.

Prepare simply: comfortable walking shoes, sun protection and weather-appropriate clothing. Compare the tastings, meals, access to particular rooms and guiding language with the confirmed itinerary. The driver must comply with restrictions on drinking alcohol; an organized transfer avoids the need to drive after tasting.

## Frequently asked questions about tours to Concha y Toro

### Is the winery visit included in the nine-day tour?

Yes. On the [Argentina and Chile wine tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-mendoza-wine-9-days/), day eight is devoted to Concha y Toro: walking through the vineyards and gardens, exploring the winery and tasting. Lunch is paid for separately.

### Can I visit only Concha y Toro, without Argentina?

The winery welcomes visitors, but the existing itinerary shown here combines Argentina and Chile. A stand-alone trip from Santiago must be arranged separately, without applying the tour's terms to it.

### Are there other wineries on the itinerary?

Yes. Before Chile, the route includes [Mendoza wine country](/argentina/place/mendoza/) and the [Uco Valley](/argentina/place/uco-valley/), allowing travelers to compare winemaking in both countries.

### Is lunch included at Concha y Toro?

Lunch on the winery grounds can be ordered for an additional charge. The other tasting and gastronomic services depend on the confirmed version of the trip.
